subject: Right-sizing renewal: commit cap, per-token ladder and uplift guardrails
messages:
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmefinance.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Upcoming renewal — right-sizing commit & discount ladder

Hi Olga,

Hope youre well. Our contract with Redwood is coming up for renewal on 2027-04-01 and wed like to discuss a plan that locks predictable unit economics for our product teams while making sure we arent pushed into an oversized commit.

A few things from our side:
- Actual hosted API usage for the last 12 months has been spiky; median month is ~130M tokens and peak months hit ~420M. We expect steady growth but with seasonal spikes.
- Were comfortable moving to a committed model if the uplift vs current run-rate is reasonable (+10-25%) and there are clear per-token breakpoints.
- Procurement needs a cap on renewal uplift (we can accept up to +20% on committed spend if offset by steeper per-token discounts and a clear true-up).

Can you share a proposed tiered per-token discount ladder and a recommended commit that balances our risk? Ive attached a usage export for your forecasting. Also looping in procurement for timelines.

Thanks,
Tom Rivera
Head of Platform, Acme Financial

Attachment: acme_usage_q1_2027.csv (csv, 120KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Upcoming renewal — right-sizing commit & discount ladder

Forwarding Acmes ask. Tom is explicitly asking for: (1) a commit recommendation that doesnt force them to over-commit in peak months, (2) a hard uplift cap (procurement prefers +20% max), and (3) aggressive per-token breaks at higher volumes. Theyve provided token-level history — attached.

High level Im thinking: propose a 12-month commit with monthly true-up, offer a soft ramp (lower initial commit + auto-trueup) and a tiered discount ladder that becomes meaningful post 500M/month aggregated (i.e., 500M, 1B, 2B token thresholds). Need to know finance approval for >20% effective discount and whether we can set an uplift guardrail in the SOW.

Can you two sketch 2 pricing scenarios (conservative & growth) and flag approvals needed? Ill own external comms.

- Olga

Quoted message below.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Upcoming renewal — right-sizing commit & discount ladder

Thanks, Olga. I put together two scenarios (attached): conservative and upside. Key points:

- Conservative: 12-month commit at ~1.2B tokens (roughly +18% vs their 12-month run-rate). Discounts: 0% <500M, 10% 500M-1B, 18% 1B-2B, 25% >2B. Monthly true-up with quarterly reporting. This keeps us protected on unit economics; pricing falls within standard commercial guidelines (no finance escalation).

- Upside (accelerated growth): 12-month commit at 1.6B tokens (+30% run-rate) with steeper breaks: 12% at 500M, 22% at 1B, 32% at 2B. This requires approval for an effective starting discount >20% and a one-time sales credit margin concession.

- Uplift guardrail: procurement asked for a hard cap on renewal uplift. We can offer an explicit "uplift limit" in the renewal SOW (e.g., max +25% on committed spend year-over-year), but anything <25% must be signed off by Finance and Sales Ops for credits. If procurement demands <=20%, we should try conservative scenario.

- True-up mechanics: monthly usage reporting, 30-day reconciliation window, overage billed at negotiated per-token rates. Consider a capped overage band (e.g., up to 10% over monthly commit at a small premium) to cover spikes.

Ive attached an XLSX with modelled P&L and margin impact. Ask: Lauren/Monica, can you confirm whether we have approval for the Upside scenario (effective >20% discount) or if we need to limit to Conservative? If finance requires >30% margin protection, we should not offer tier >32%.

Attachment: pricing_scenarios.xlsx (xlsx)

Ben

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmefinance.com>, procurement@acmefinance.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — right-sizing commit & discount ladder

Tom / Procurement team,

Thanks for the context and the usage file. Weve modelled two options and wanted to share a proposal you can review quickly:

Option A (Conservative, Finance-friendly)
- 12-month committed spend: 1.2B tokens
- Per-token discount ladder (effective compared to list):
  - 0% for first 500M tokens
  - 10% for 500M-1B
  - 18% for 1B-2B
  - 25% beyond 2B
- Monthly true-up with quarterly crediting; capped monthly overage allowance = 10% at +15% premium rate.
- Renewal uplift guardrail: max +20% on committed annual spend (per your ask). If they exceed this at renewal, any uplift >20% is subject to review and potential step-down credits.

Option B (Growth-aligned, Sales-approved pending finance)
- 12-month committed spend: 1.6B tokens
- Per-token discount ladder:
  - 10% at 500M
  - 20% at 1B
  - 30% at 2B
- Monthly true-up; dedicated onboarding support and 30-day SLA crediting built in.
- Renewal uplift guardrail: max +25% (requires Finance approval).

We can provide an illustrative invoice schedule and a draft SOW that explicitly captures the uplift cap and true-up mechanics. If procurement is comfortable with Option A, well prepare a redline-ready SOW and a DocuSign envelope. Option B is available if they can sign off on the larger commit and allow Finance to approve the effective discount.

Link: https://docs.redwood.com/shared/RI_term_summary.pdf (term summary draft)

Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RI_term_summary.pdf (pdf)
